speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you are presenting with chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative colitis (likely flaring due to infection trigger or coincidental camp exposure). The clinical picture—chronic diarrhea, relief with defecation, urgency, mucus, and tenesmus—strongly supports inflammatory bowel disease over infectious etiologies given the 4-month duration, though Campylobacter or other pathogens must be ruled out.

REQUEST TEST: Stool culture, O&P, C. diff toxin, and fecal calprotectin.
REQUEST IMAGES: Colonoscopy with biopsy.
